title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: Interrelated components working together to collect, process, store and disseminate information to support decision-making.
The use of computers, storage, networking and other devices, infrastructure and processes to create, process, store, secure and exchange electronic data.

en.text: An information system is a set of interrelated components that collect, process, store and disseminate information to support decisions. Its use raises ethical and legal issues (privacy, digital ownership, information gathering, security), social issues (socialization gaps, cyberbullying, addiction, plagiarism, cybercrime, jobs), environmental issues (e-waste, green technology) and health issues. The unit also covers intellectual property rights, digital identity management, digital collaboration and digital citizenship.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Ethical and legal issues: privacy, digital ownership, information gathering, security and liability.
Social issues: socialization gaps, cyberbullying, addiction, plagiarism, cybercrime, jobs.
Environmental and health issues: e-waste, green technology, posture, eyes, sleep.
Intellectual property: trade secrets, patents, copyrights, trademarks.
Digital identity management and the National ID.
Digital citizenship: responsible, active use of technology.

notes.text: Review Part I Q5 is missing a word: "...systems that can make proper and ethical use of information systems". With "use" added it is True; the lesson rewords it.
Review Part II Q2 is flawed: A, B and C can all be collected or inferred from purchases, and the unit does not teach this. The lesson changes option D "None" to "All of these" (the answer).

Review Part II Q3: the term "Environmental Information System" never appears in the unit; students can only answer by elimination. Part II Q5 is ambiguous ("inventions, discoveries" are patents); the lesson rewords it to "expressions of ideas and creations, like art and writing" (copyright).

Part III discussion questions are turned into pick and mcq items; Part IV (group case study) is a project and is not graded. There is no national-exam IT item bank yet, so the chapter test draws from the section tests.
